newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes ease, buyers take imports.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes ease, buyers take imports.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes drifted lower Thursday, as crude oil futures fell and discounts remained stable amid an absense of buyers, traders said.

West Coast buyerss attributed the lack of interest to cheaper imports and weaker crude oil prices on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX), which tested technical support by falling as low as $19.38 a barrel early Thursday.
Alaska North Slope (ANS), the West Coast benchmark, slipped five cents from Wednesday to $18.38/18.58 a barrel in line with NYMEX crude markets.
"I have not been focused on buying any crudes with the market going down," one crude trader said.
Some refiners were already supplied for May.
Chevron West Coast refiners will take four cargoes of Ecuadorian crude over the next two months, and Shell has bought a cargo of Cano Limon crude, according to some traders.
ANS, which buyers say will fall in value, is now priced at $1.02 off West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the bellweather U.S. grade traded on NYMEX.
"Imports should be severe over the next couple weeks," one California trader said.
California heavy grades were flat Thursday, after falling Wednesday as major oil companies lower prices.
Kern River, a representative heavy crude, has fallen over $4 since January and continues to come under pressure from WTI, traders said.
